newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Africa work to boost LTA yr shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Africa work to boost LTA yr shr.

text.p: A heavy work schedule in South Africa and in other African countries was seen boosting construction and engineering firm LTA Ltd's year earnings, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said LTA, which is 68.4 percent owned by Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd, was likely to lift earnings to between 189 and 191 cents for the year to December 31 with consensus at 190.2 -- a 17 percent rise on a year ago.
The poll showed analysts expected a dividend of around 66.6 cents a share, up from 57.5 before.
LTA is due to report results on Monday.
"Last year was a pretty good year for LTA because they had a lot of contracts inside as well as outside the country," said Mike Haworth, an analyst at BoE NatWest.

"Involvement in the Lesotho Highlands Water Project, the building of arterial roads inside South Africa and an interest in the Saldanha Steel Project must have helped them for the past year," Haworth told Reuters.
Analysts said expected growth in African economies this year and an increase in construction and engineering work there pointed to a bright future for LTA.
"LTA is sailing nicely into Africa," said Nolan Menachemson, an analyst at SMK Securities.
Menachemson said open cast mining operations was also seen a major contributor to LTA's earnings.

Analysts said LTA also stood to benefit in the long term from low-cost housing developments, through which President Nelson Mandela's government is hoping to redress South Africa's acute housing shortage.
"They (LTA) are quite likely to participate in low-cost housing. It's got to happen sometime," said Sean Jelley, an analyst at SBC Warburg.
